'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
***[[List of drone strikes in Afghanistan]]
****The [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] says that a [[drone strike]] conducted on [[August 2021 Kabul drone strike|August 29]] that killed 10 Afghan civilians was not a result of criminal [[negligence]], nor did it violate the [[law of war]]. [https://www.businessinsider.in/politics/world/news/pentagon-watchdog-says-drone-strike-that-killed-10-afghan-civilians-including-7-kids-didnt-violate-the-laws-of-war/articleshow/87518069.cms (''Business Insider India'')]
*[[Mapuche conflict]]
**Two [[indigenous peoples|indigenous]] [[Mapuche]] people are killed and three more are injured in clashes with [[Chilean Army|Chilean soldiers]] in [[Arauco Province]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/4/two-mapuche-die-in-clashes-with-chilean-security-forces (Al Jazeera)] 
*[[Algeria–Morocco relations#2021|2021 Algeria–Morocco crisis]]
**[[Algeria]] accuses [[Moroccan Armed Forces]] of being behind a [[truck bombing]] at the border area between [[Mauritania]] and the [[International recognition of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic|disputed territory]] of [[Western Sahara]] two days ago, killing three [[Algerians|Algerian]] citizens. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/3/three-algerians-killed-in-attack-presidency-blames-on-morocco (Al Jazeera)]
*[[War crimes in the Tigray War]]
**A [[United Nations]] report accuses all sides in the [[Tigray War]] of committing [[war crime]]s on civilians, including [[torture]], [[extrajudicial killing]]s, [[gang rape]]s and arrests based on [[ethnic groups in Ethiopia|ethnicity]]. The head of the [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|Human Rights office]], [[Michelle Bachelet]], especially accused the [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|forces of Ethiopia]] and [[Eritrean Defence Forces|Eritrea]] for most of the [[human rights in Ethiopia|human rights]] violations. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/03/possible-war-crimes-on-all-sides-in-ethiopian-conflict-report-tigray (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Mass media in Iran|Iranian state media]] reports that the [[United States Navy]] attempted to capture an Iranian [[oil tanker]]. The oil tanker was boarded, commandeered and then returned by [[Iranian Navy|Iranian]] [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy|NEDSA]] marines in a helicopter operation. [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. officials]] refute the report, saying that the Iranians had captured a [[Vietnam|Vietnamese]] flagged tanker and that [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. forces]] were monitoring the situation. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-state-tv-says-iran-thwarts-us-attempt-steal-oil-sea-oman-2021-11-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
**Around 40 fighters storm the city of [[Bukavu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], singing songs calling for the liberation of the country and opening fire against [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|security forces]], killing two soldiers and a police officer. Six attackers are killed and 36 others are arrested. [https://news.trust.org/item/20211103123914-vhzbg/ (Thomson Reuters Foundation)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021 global energy crisis]]
**[[2021 United Kingdom natural gas supplier crisis]]
***Six more [[Energy industry|private energy providers]] collapse in the [[United Kingdom]] amid rising [[natural gas]] prices, including CNG Energy, affecting around 41,000 customers. There are now fears that [[Bulb Energy]], which supplies around 1.7 million people, could be at risk of imminent collapse. [https://metro.co.uk/2021/11/03/energy-crisis-uk-cng-energy-collapses-affecting-over-40000-customers-15536748/ (''Metro'')]
*The [[United States Department of Commerce|U.S. Commerce Department]] adds Israeli [[spyware]] firms [[Candiru (spyware company)|Candiru]] and [[NSO Group]] to its trade blacklist for selling their services and tools to foreign governments to spy on government officials and journalists, and for trafficking tools used to hack computer networks respectively. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/us-blacklists-four-companies-israel-russia-singapore-citing-spyware-2021-11-03/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Lagos high-rise collapse]]
**The death toll from the [[structural integrity and failure|collapse]] of a [[high-rise building]] under [[construction]] in [[Ikoyi]], [[Lagos]], [[Nigeria]], increases to 22, as the [[search-and-rescue]] operations enter their third day. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/3/death-toll-climbs-to-22-in-nigeria-building-collapse (Al Jazeera)]
*A passenger bus [[Bus plunge|plunges]] down a ravine in [[Azad Kashmir]], [[Pakistan]], killing at least 22 people. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1655714 (''Dawn'')]
*A [[Belarus|Belarusian]]-owned [[Antonov An-12]] [[cargo plane]] [[crash-land]]s in [[Siberia]], killing all nine people on board. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/nine-killed-in-cargo-plane-crash-in-siberia (Reuters via ''The Straits Times'')]
*A magnitude 5.7 [[list of earthquakes in Argentina|earthquake]] strikes [[Mendoza Province]], [[Argentina]], near [[Argentina–Chile border|the border]] with [[Chile]] at 00:17 [[Time in Argentina|ART]]. No casualties are reported but minimal damage to buildings is reported. [https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/earthquakes/quake-info/6478721/quake-alert-Nov-3-2021-Chile.html (VolcanoDiscovery)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Metro Manila]]
*****The [[Metropolitan Manila Development Authority#Metro Manila Council|Metro Manila Council]] approves the lifting of the unified curfew over the [[Metro Manila|National Capital Region]], which was instituted in March 2020, beginning tomorrow. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/no-more-metro-manila-curfew-starting-november-4-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Saudi Arabia]]
****The [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] Food and Drug Authority approves the usage of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 5 and 11 years old. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1961011/saudi-arabia (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
****The [[Italian Medicines Agency]] recommends that anyone that received the [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine]] should receive a booster dose of either the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer]] or [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccines six months after they received their first dose due to a slow decline of efficacy against mild and moderate forms of the disease. [https://news.yahoo.com/italy-recommends-pfizer-moderna-booster-140459956.html (Yahoo! News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,189 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] from [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 242,060. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/russia-logs-40443-covid-19-cases-in-past-24-hours20211103142210 (Asian News International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] reports a record 3,456 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [http://famagusta-gazette.com/2021/11/04/slovenias-daily-count-of-covid-19-cases-hits-new-high/?fbclid=IwAR1u5_Xygoc6omdks3MNSgYmorjOSe2g-XRz6m6wDHr4gX3jy1vhdadBVH4 (Famagusta Gazette)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Rady Children's Hospital]] in [[San Diego]] administers the first vaccines to children between the ages of 5 and 11 years old after [[Pfizer]]'s COVID-19 vaccine was approved for use in children by the [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]]. [https://www.cbs8.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/vaccine/rady-childrens-delivers-first-covid-19-shots-for-kids-ages-5-to-11/509-3a539ebb-6898-432e-81fa-540d658b0789 (KFMB-TV)]
***The United States begins administering the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] to children between ages of 5 and 11 years old nationwide. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2021/11/03/first-kids-5-11-covid-vaccines/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[World Health Organization]] approves an emergency use listing for the [[Covaxin]] COVID-19 vaccine manufactured by the Indian biotech firm [[Bharat Biotech]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/covaxin-bharat-biotechs-india-made-covid-vaccine-cleared-by-who-sources-2598395 (NDTV)]
*[[2020–2021 H5N8 outbreak]]
**The [[World Organization for Animal Health]] reports an outbreak of the highly pathogenic [[H5N1]] [[bird flu]] at a turkey farm in [[Slagelse]], [[Denmark]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/denmark-reports-outbreak-bird-flu-turkey-farm-oie-2021-11-03/ (Reuters)]
*The [[United Kingdom]] declares nationwide Avian Influenza Prevention Zone and orders bird-keepers to follow strict biosecurity measures after a number of cases of the disease were detected in wild [[bird]]s. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/bird-flu-uk-2021-prevention-zone-b1950903.html (''The Independent'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–Poland relations]]
**[[Censorship in Belarus]]
***[[Belarus]] declares the [[Poland|Polish]] [[free-to-air]] television channel [[Belsat TV]] an "extremist organisation", which could result in its employees and viewers facing up to seven years in prison. The network is banned in Belarus, though its viewers have continued to access it via the [[internet]] and [[Virtual private network|VPNs]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-declares-poland-based-belsat-news-channel-an-extremist-organisation-2021-11-03/ (Reuters)]
**Poland summons the Belarusian [[chargé d'affaires]] after [[Belarusian Ground Forces|Belarusian troops]] crossed into Polish territory overnight. A [[Polish government]] spokesman says that the Belarusian personnel advanced {{convert|300|m|ft}} into Poland and only returned across [[Belarus–Poland border|the border]] when they were confronted by a Polish patrol. [https://www.dw.com/en/poland-summons-belarus-envoy-over-armed-border-incursion/a-59708702 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Foreign relations of Antigua and Barbuda]], [[Foreign relations of Tuvalu]]
**A lawyer representing the governments of [[Antigua and Barbuda]] and [[Tuvalu]] says that a new commission is being formed to sue big polluters and claim damage reparations for [[climate change]] effects on those nations before the [[International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/climate-change-antigua-barbuda-tuvalu-lawsuit-polluters/ (CBS News)]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**Deputy [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian Foreign Minister]] [[Ali Bagheri]] announces that negotiations to revive the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]] will begin on [[November 29]] in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/3/iran-nuclear-talks-with-world-powers-to-resume-on-november-29 (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 United States elections]]
**[[2021 United States gubernatorial elections]]
***[[2021 New Jersey gubernatorial election]]
****Incumbent [[Governor of New Jersey|New Jersey Governor]] [[Phil Murphy]] defeats [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former state legislator [[Jack Ciattarelli]], making him the first [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] to be re-elected since [[Brendan Byrne]] in [[1977 New Jersey gubernatorial election|1977]]. [https://www.nj.com/politics/2021/11/murphy-wins-bruising-nj-governors-race-narrowly-beating-ciattarelli-for-2nd-term.html (NJ)] [https://apnews.com/article/elections-new-jersey-voter-registration-election-2020-phil-murphy-770588f9859dca14e8c186bc5020d553 (Associated Press)]
*[[Corruption in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] votes to approve a [[government of the United Kingdom|government]]-sanctioned amendment to replace the [[Commons Select Committee on Standards]]. The vote means that [[Conservative Party (UK)|Tory]] MP [[Owen Paterson]] will avoid a 30-day suspension from parliament over an "egregious breach" of [[lobbying]] rules. The vote was widely condemned by opposition parties. [https://news.sky.com/story/owen-paterson-govt-backed-axing-of-standards-committee-will-be-condemned-as-tory-stitch-up-12459037 (Sky News)]
